cards.existing: Six person endings: -ю (yu)/-у (я, ya = I), -ешь (ты, ty = you), -ет (он/она = he/she), -ем (мы = we), -ете (вы = you pl), -ют (они = they).

cards.existing: Subject pronouns: я (ya = I), ты (ty = you), он (on = he), она (ona = she), мы (my = we), вы (vy = you pl), они (oni = they). Keep them in.

cards.existing: Perfective verb forms (often with prefixes like `по-`, `про-`, `с-`, `на-`) describe completed, one-time actions: `я прочитал книгу` (I read [and finished] the book).

cards.existing: Russian has two 'you's: `ты` (informal – family, friends, kids) and `вы` (formal – strangers, elders, work, and plural for everyone). They use different verb forms: `ты говоришь` vs `вы говорите`.

cards.existing: Past tense often signals aspect by the prefix: bare verb (impf, ongoing) vs prefixed verb (pf, completed). `Я писал письмо` (I was writing) vs `я написал письмо` (I wrote and finished).

cards.existing: `Где` vs `куда` vs `откуда`: location vs destination vs origin. `Где ты?` (Where are you?) vs `куда ты идёшь?` (Where are you going?). English uses 'where' for both.
